title: Speciation peaks during elevation, but fossil deposits form mainly during subsidence

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Speciation peaks during elevation, but fossil deposits form mainly during subsidence

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Periods of land elevation favour the formation of new varieties and species but leave little geological record, whereas periods of subsidence bring much extinction and fewer new species yet produce most fossil-rich deposits, so transitional forms are seldom recorded.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: consequently during subsidence, though there will be much extinction, fewer new varieties or species will be formed; and it is during these very periods of subsidence, that our great deposits rich in fossils have been accumulated.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On the intermittence of geological formations”. Scope: coastal and shallow-marine faunas and their fossil record

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing databases support broad temporal association tests. Preservation bias is entangled with the proposed biological rates, limiting causal discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Align regional uplift and subsidence histories with origination, extinction, and fossil-deposition rates, correcting for sampling. Elevation-associated origination and subsidence-associated extinction and fossil richness support the linked prediction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Rock availability directly biases inferred diversity rates.

Elevation and subsidence are spatially heterogeneous and difficult to align with populations.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.62
data existence: 0.88

discriminating power: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Origination, extinction, and the stratigraphic context of fossil-rich rock are all in public databases, and the correlation has a standard form. Sampling bias that moves with sea level is severe enough that the same pattern is predicted without any change in true speciation, so discriminating power stays limited. The test also substitutes marine genera for the varieties and coastal species in the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare per-capita origination and extinction of shallow-marine genera between intervals independently classed as regional uplift and as subsidence, and ask whether fossil-rich rock is concentrated in the subsidence bins. Higher origination during elevation and higher extinction plus richer deposits during subsidence would support the coupling; the reverse pattern would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Varieties and coastal faunas are poorly resolved compared with marine shelly genera.

The amount of preserved rock covaries with sea level, so apparent speciation and extinction track sampling.

Uplift intervals are exactly when the record is worst, so the predicted speciation peak is hardest to see.
